eval.title: Amazon Stock Is Another Better & Better Buy (Risk & Reward Valuation)

call.headline_quote: I think that it is a medium short term but low long-term risk if you invest in Amazon now

base_metric.name: net_income
base_metric.quote: 10 on 500 billion and more it's 50 billion in valuation or 55 billion with the last earnings

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: if we take 55 billion on the 900 billion market cap the price earnings ratio for Amazon is 16

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: if I add the 20 billion of stock compensation then the profits the estimated potential is not 55 billion and the p ratio goes to 30 which is then not as cheap

reasons.claim: On an assumed 10% net margin, Amazon trades at a P/E of only 16 for a business he thinks can double again in five years.
reasons.quote: and if we take 55 billion on the 900 billion market cap the price earnings ratio for Amazon is 16.

data_check.gap_note: he says 9e+11, as-of 4.57998e+10 (FY2021); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: estimated net margin, implied net income, implied pe

reasons.claim: Heavy stock-based compensation dilution means the real earnings power is lower, pushing the effective P/E up to 30.
reasons.quote: then again as I mentioned already if I add the 20 billion of stock compensation then the profits the estimated potential is not 55 billion and the p ratio goes to 30

data_check.gap_note: he says 20, as-of 89.98 (2022-11-08); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: adjusted pe

reasons.claim: Despite the stock crashing, the underlying business is still growing strongly, including AWS.
reasons.quote: the stock is down but sales are up 19 that is still remarkable the business is still growing

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: AWS growth

reasons.claim: Management says the current margin and cash flow pressure is temporary and expects a recovery as capex and inventory efficiency improve.
reasons.quote: we expect to see a recovery in income generation normalization of the inventory versus accounts payable cycle and efficiency in our capex spend we intend to flip those numbers around

reasons.claim: Weak guidance and a myopic, panicked market could push the stock down another 30-40% short term even though he thinks it's a good long-term buy.
reasons.quote: the stock can go down another 30 percent very very easily

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: potential further downside

external_facts_used: Amazon shifted ~$10bn spending from fulfillment to AWS capex
Stock-based compensation expense of $5.6bn in the quarter (>$20bn annualized)
AWS outage in September took down his own research platform, illustrating how widely AWS is used
Analyst questions from Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan on the earnings call focused on revenue guidance and cash flow/margins
